subject.title: Session Routing Bugs: CLI routing to wrong session, WeChat ID inconsistency, and session deadlock from message flooding

question: Should #88204 stay as a tracking umbrella, or should maintainers split and route each reported session-routing failure to focused canonical issues now?
rationale: The current evidence spans multiple owner boundaries and at least two product semantics decisions: default TUI session identity and what counts as meaningful session activity versus background churn.

options.title: Split and route now
options.body: Use #51028 for activity ordering, #93255 for sessions_send channel routing, #90178/#86538 for subagent deadlock overlaps, and create focused follow-ups for the TUI default and WeChat live repro gaps.

options.title: Keep umbrella as tracker
options.body: Leave #88204 open as the cross-cutting coordination issue, but require maintainers to mark which subproblem owns acceptance criteria before any fix PR is queued.

options.title: Close only after canonicals land
options.body: Wait to close this umbrella until the open canonical issues are merged or maintainers explicitly decide the remaining WeChat/flood claims are out of scope.

recommendation.title: Split and route now
recommendation.body: Use #51028 for activity ordering, #93255 for sessions_send channel routing, #90178/#86538 for subagent deadlock overlaps, and create focused follow-ups for the TUI default and WeChat live repro gaps.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-boundary product triage decision, and steipete is the strongest sourced project-level decision owner in CONTRIBUTING and current source history.
